mnAdditions.description: M1 line 2: Schedule M1M line 10 + M1MB line 9 additions (non-MN municipal bond interest, federal bonus-depreciation/§ 179 addbacks, positive M1NC adjustments — Minnesota's IRC is frozen at May 1, 2023, so 2025 OBBBA items convert on Schedule M1NC)

mnAdvanceCtcRepayment.description: M1 line 14b: repayment of 2025 ADVANCE Child Tax Credit payments elected on the 2024 return (reconciliation, NEW for 2025)

mnAmt.description: M1 line 11: Schedule M1MT alternative minimum tax (6.75% broadened base, agent-computed — REQUIRED whenever AMT preference items exist; disclose)

mnAppliedToNextYear.description: M1 line 30: refund applied to 2026 estimated tax

mnDependentEarnedIncome.description: dependent-claimed filer's earned income for the dependent standard-deduction worksheet (lesser of the table amount or max($1,250, earned + $350))

mnDependents.description: dependents on Schedule M1DQC — $5,200 each (2025), phased 2% per $2,500 ceil-step of AGI over $358,550 MFJ/QSS, $239,050 single, $298,800 HOH, $179,275 MFS (gone once the excess passes $122,500/$61,250-MFS); $0 for dependent-claimed filers

mnItemized.description: Schedule M1SA Minnesota itemized deductions AFTER M1SA's own 3%/10%/80% limitation — the composer takes the larger of this or the computed standard deduction (MFS: standard barred when the spouse itemizes; pass mnMfsSpouseItemizes)

mnMfsSpouseItemizes.description: MFS only: the other spouse claims Minnesota itemized deductions — bars the standard deduction (the composer then requires mnItemized)

mnNetInvestmentIncome.description: Schedule NIIT Minnesota net investment income (federal 8960 concept minus class 2a agricultural-land gains) — the composer evaluates us.mn.niit (1% over $1,000,000) into line 14a

mnOtherTaxes14a.description: M1 line 14a: M1HOME/M1529 recapture, M1LS lump-sum tax, and the Schedule NIIT amount if computed outside the composer

mnPenaltyInterest.description: M1 line 28: late-filing/late-payment penalty and interest (agent-computed per the instructions)

mnRrTier1Offset.description: Tier 1 Railroad Retirement benefits already subtracted on M1M line 17 — the SS worksheet (steps 25-29) reduces the simplified-method subtraction by this amount (no double subtraction)

mnSsAlternativeMethod.description: the M1M Worksheet ALTERNATIVE-method Social Security subtraction (steps 9-28, agent-computed, NET of the Tier 1 RR offset) — the composer takes the GREATER of this and the oracle simplified method when AGI exceeds the full-subtraction threshold (2025 alternative maxes: $5,840 MFJ/QSS, $4,560 single/HOH, $2,920 MFS)

mnStateRefund.description: M1 line 6: state income tax refund from federal Schedule 1 line 1 (its own subtraction line)

mnStdBoxes.description: 65-or-older (born before January 2, 1961) and blind boxes for you/spouse — each adds $2,000 (single/HOH) or $1,550 (married statuses) to the standard deduction

mnSubtractions.description: M1 line 7 subtractions (M1M line 40 + M1MB line 22) EXCLUDING the composer-computed Social Security subtraction: U.S. government interest, K-12 education expenses, charitable over $500 for non-itemizers (50% of the excess), bonus-depreciation recovery, M1R age-65+/disabled, M1QPEN public pension, military items, the new 2025 items (coerced debt, consumer enforcement, foreign service, SEIU stipends)

mnUnderpaymentPenalty.description: M1 line 27: Schedule M15 underpayment penalty

mnWildlifeContribution.description: M1 line 18: Nongame Wildlife Fund contribution (reduces the refund)

mo529Deposit.description: MO-1040 line 52: refund deposited to a Missouri 529 (MOST) account (minimum $25, Form 5632)

moActiveDutyMilitary.description: MO-1040 line 18: active duty military income deduction (100%, incl. annual training and — NEW 2025 — National Guard/reserve signing bonuses)

moAdditionsSpouse.description: MO-A Part 1 line 7S: the spouse's additions

moAdditionsYou.description: MO-A Part 1 line 7Y: the primary's additions (non-Missouri state/local bond interest, PTE/NOL addbacks, nonqualified 529/ABLE distributions, food pantry, nonresident property tax)

moAppliedToNextYear.description: MO-1040 line 50: overpayment applied to 2026 estimated tax

moBusinessIncomeSpouse.description: the spouse's net business income for the 20% deduction (17S)

moBusinessIncomeYou.description: the primary's MISSOURI-SOURCE net business income per the p.16 worksheet (Schedule C line 31 + Schedule E line 32 + Schedule F/4835 profits, losses netted, MINUS agricultural disaster relief payments already on MO-A line 16; $0 if net loss) — the composer takes the 20% § 143.022 deduction (MO-A line 17Y)

moCapitalGainSpouse.description: the spouse's share of federal capital gains for the 100% subtraction

moCapitalGainYou.description: the primary's share of federally reported capital gains (Form 1040 line 7a) — the composer subtracts 100% (MO-A line 18, H.B. 594, NEW for TY2025; a negative amount enters as $0)

moEnterpriseZoneYou.description: MO-1040 line 28Y: enterprise zone / rural empowerment zone income modification

moFagiSpouse.description: MO-1040 line 1S: the spouse's share of federal AGI (combined returns). 1Y + 1S must equal the federal AGI. A NEGATIVE share triggers the 12 CSR 10-2.710 zeroing the composer applies (negative spouse $0, other spouse the netted joint FAGI; both $0 when combined FAGI is negative).

moFagiYou.description: MO-1040 line 1Y: the PRIMARY taxpayer's share of federal AGI — Missouri combined returns SPLIT total FAGI between spouses per the AGI worksheet (each spouse's own income; joint items allocated). Defaults to the full federalAGI when omitted (one-income couple).

moFederalItemized.description: MO-A Part 2 line 1: total federal itemized deductions (federal Schedule A total) plus any approved cultural contributions (literary/musical/scholastic/artistic donations, § 143.141)

moFederalTax9.description: MO-1040 line 9 'Tax from federal return': federal 1040 line 22 MINUS lines 27a and 29, MINUS Schedule 2 Part 1 line 3, MINUS Schedule 3 Part 2 line 9 — never withholding; the EIC must be subtracted

moHcsmDeduction.description: MO-1040 line 17: health care sharing ministry contributions not deducted federally

moInactiveDutyMilitary.description: MO-1040 line 19: inactive duty (drill) military income deduction

moItemizing.description: taxpayer itemized FEDERALLY and wants Missouri itemized deductions — the composer computes MO-A Part 2 (federal itemized + payroll-tax addback − net state income taxes) and takes the LARGER of that or the standard deduction unless moRequiredToItemize

moLtcDeduction.description: MO-1040 line 16: qualified long-term care insurance premiums (12+ month policies, net of federally deducted amounts, per the worksheet)

moNetStateIncomeTaxes.description: MO-A Part 2 line 11: state/local income taxes from Schedule A line 5a MINUS Kansas City/St. Louis earnings taxes (which stay deductible) — or the Part 2 worksheet result when SALT exceeded $40,000/$20,000-MFS or FAGI exceeded $500,000/$250,000-MFS

moNrPayments.description: MO-1040 lines 39+40: MO-2NR/MO-2ENT nonresident partner/entertainer payments

moOtherDeductions.description: MO-1040 lines 21-24 bucket: beginning farmer, transport facility, foster parent deductions (agent-transcribed)

moOtherFederalTax10.description: MO-1040 line 10 'Other federal tax': Schedule 2 Part 1 line 3 + Part 2 lines 8/14/15 + recapture in line 21 + Schedule 3 Part 1 line 1 (attach 4255/8611/8828 for recapture)

moOtherTaxesYou.description: MO-1040 line 34Y: 10% of the Federal Form 4972 lump-sum distribution tax, and/or recapture of the low income housing credit (Form 8611) — the printed checkboxes. (Form 4970 trust accumulation amounts are a SUBTRACTION, not a line 34 tax.)

moPayrollTaxAddback.description: MO-A Part 2 lines 2-7 total: the 2025 employee Social Security tax (capped $10,918 per spouse), Railroad Retirement Tier I+II (capped $17,327 per spouse, net of employer refunds), Medicare tax (with Form 8959 adjustments), and self-employment tax (Schedule 2 line 4 − Schedule 1 line 15 + Form 8959 line 13) — Missouri ADDS payroll taxes into itemized deductions

moPrivatePensionSpouse.description: the spouse's private-source pension for Section B

moPrivatePensionYou.description: the primary's PRIVATE-source taxable pension/annuity/IRA/401(k) (1040 lines 4b+5b share) — Section B caps each spouse at $6,000 and phases out by income

moPropertyTaxCredit.description: MO-1040 line 43: Form MO-PTS property tax credit (refundable circuit breaker — actual property tax up to $1,100 owners / 20%-of-rent up to $750 renters, from the printed chart; net household income gates $30,000 owners / $27,200 renters; agent-computed from MO-PTS with disclosure)

moPublicPensionSpouse.description: the spouse's public-source pension for their Section A column

moPublicPensionYou.description: the primary's PUBLIC-source pension (federal/state/local government, 1040 line 5b share) — the composer runs MO-A Part 3 Section A (min(pension, $47,633) less their Section C exemption). Military retirement goes in moSubtractionsYou instead (100%, MO-A line 10).

moRequiredToItemize.description: the filer was REQUIRED to itemize federally (e.g. MFS with an itemizing spouse) — Missouri then requires itemizing even when the standard deduction is larger

moResidentCreditYou.description: MO-1040 line 31Y: Form MO-CR credit for taxes paid to other states (agent-computed; the composer caps at line 30Y)

moSsExemptSpouse.description: the spouse's Section C SS/SSD exemption on the same gates

moSsExemptYou.description: the primary's MO-A Section C exemption: their TAXABLE Social Security/SSD (1040 line 6b share), 100% exempt — pass ONLY if 62+ by December 31 (the MO-1040 age box) or on Social Security Disability (attested)

moStandardDeductionOverride.description: dependent-claimed filers: the federal DEPENDENT standard deduction limit (greater of $1,350 or earned income + $450, capped at the full amount) — replaces the composer's full standard deduction

moSubtractionsSpouse.description: the spouse's MO-A subtractions on the same terms

moSubtractionsYou.description: MO-A subtractions for the primary EXCLUDING the composer-computed capital gain (line 18) and business income deduction (line 17): exempt federal-obligation interest, state refund, military retirement (100%), railroad retirement, 529/ABLE contributions ($8,000/taxpayer), qualified health insurance premiums, depreciation adjustments, agriculture disaster relief

moTrustFundDonations.description: MO-1040 line 51: trust fund donations total (51a-51l)

moUnderpaymentPenalty.description: MO-1040 line 55: Form MO-2210 underpayment penalty (90% / 66⅔%-farmer safe harbors)

moWftcInvestmentOver4400.description: Form MO-WFTC question 3: investment income exceeds $4,400 — denies the credit. The MO credit follows EIC law FROZEN as of January 1, 2021 (MO-1040 instructions p.10), so this is the indexed pre-ARPA limit; compute investment income the pre-2021 way (taxable AND tax-exempt interest, dividends, positive net capital gain per the MO-WFTC instructions), NOT the current federal $11,950 gate.

mt529Deposit.description: Form 2 line 25: amount of the refund deposited into a 529 or 529A account (must exceed $25 per account)

mtAbleContributions.description: Schedule I line 17: contributions to an ABLE account — capped at $3,000, or $6,000 on a JOINT return. Not inflation-indexed

mtActiveDutyMilitaryPay.description: Schedule I line 12: active-duty military salary, subtracted in full (§ 15-30-2120(3)(c)) — basic, special and incentive pay only. Annual training, inactive duty training and 'active Guard and Reserve duty' pay do NOT qualify

mtAge62.description: Schedule 2EC: the claimant reached age 62 by December 31 — required for the elderly homeowner/renter credit (unattested → not claimed)

mtAmendedPaymentsWithOriginal.description: Form 2 line 18 (amended returns): payments made with the original return

mtAppliedToNextYear.description: Form 2 line 24: amount of the overpayment applied to 2026 estimated taxes

mtExemptTribalIncome.description: Schedule I line 11: exempt tribal income of an enrolled member living on the reservation of their tribe (Form ETM)

mtFederalDeductions.description: REQUIRED for Montana. Form 2 line 2: the total of federal Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b — the federal standard OR itemized deduction plus the Schedule 1-A deductions (qualified tips, qualified overtime, passenger vehicle loan interest, the enhanced senior deduction). Montana has NO standard deduction of its own, so this is the only deduction. Do NOT include the federal qualified business income deduction — § 15-30-2120(2)(i) adds it back

mtFederalNetLongTermCapitalGains.description: Schedule III Part II line 13: federal net long-term capital gains — the denominator of the capital gains block's Montana ratio

mtGrossHouseholdIncome.description: Schedule 2EC line 18: GROSS household income — ALL income of ALL household members, taxable and non-taxable: the full amount of pensions and annuities, Railroad Retirement and veterans' disability benefits, excluded capital gains, alimony, support money, cash public assistance, tax-exempt interest, ALL Social Security, and refundable credits received in cash (expressly including the 2024 Montana property tax rebate). This is NOT federal AGI. Must be under $45,000

mtLoanOutWithholding.description: Form 2 line 11e: loan-out withholding from Form LOWCERT

mtMilitaryRetireeEligible.description: MCA 15-30-2120(9)(a): the retiree became a Montana resident on or after June 30, 2023, or was a resident both before and after receiving the pension (unattested → no subtraction)

mtMilitaryRetireeWithinFiveYears.description: MCA 15-30-2120(9)(b): the subtraction is within the five consecutive years allowed after first qualifying (unattested → no subtraction)

mtMilitaryRetirementIncome.description: Schedule I line 13: military pension, military retirement income or military survivor benefits (Form WMRE). The subtraction is the LESSER of Montana source wage income or 50% of this — it is for WORKING military retirees

mtMontanaSourceWageIncome.description: MCA 15-30-2120(8)(i): Montana source WAGE income, which caps the military retirement subtraction. A fully retired veteran with no wages gets $0

mtNetLongTermCapitalGains.description: Form 2 page 2 line 2: net long-term capital gains subject to the federal tax — generally the LESSER of federal Schedule D line 15 or line 16. Montana taxes these at 3% / 4.1%. Qualified dividends are NOT included: they are Montana ordinary income

mtOccupied6Months.description: Schedule 2EC: the claimant occupied a Montana residence as owner, renter or lessee at least six months during the year

mtOrdinaryIncomeSourcedToMontana.description: Schedule III Part II line 3: income sourced and taxable to Montana excluding net long-term capital gains (full-year residents: federal Form 1040 line 9 excluding those gains, less related expenses)

mtOtherStateCapitalGains.description: Schedule III Part II line 11: net long-term capital gain sourced and taxable to the other state or country

mtOtherStateOrdinaryIncome.description: Schedule III Part II line 1: income sourced and taxable to the other state or country included in Montana taxable income, EXCLUDING net long-term capital gains

mtOtherStateTaxPaid.description: Schedule III Part II lines 4 AND 14: the TOTAL income tax liability actually paid to the other state or country, excluding penalties and interest — the same figure feeds both blocks; the line 16 ratio attributes the capital-gains share. North Dakota WAGES are not eligible (reciprocity — file an ND return for a refund); foreign tax is ineligible if a federal Form 1116 credit was claimed

mtOtherStateTotalIncome.description: Schedule III Part II lines 2 and 12: ALL income sourced and taxable to the other state or country — the denominator of the first ratio

mtOutOfStateBondInterest.description: Schedule I Part I line 1: interest and mutual fund dividends from state, county or municipal bonds of states OTHER than Montana

mtPassThroughEntityTaxCredit.description: Form 2 line 11c: total pass-through entity tax credit from Montana Schedule(s) K-1, Part V line 1

mtPropertyTaxBilled.description: Schedule 2EC line 23: property tax billed on the Montana residence and up to one acre, including special assessments and fees but excluding penalties and interest

mtRailroadRetirementBenefits.description: Schedule I lines 22-23: Tier I and Tier II Railroad Retirement benefits included in federal taxable income, exempt by federal law

mtRentPaid.description: Schedule 2EC line 24: rent paid for the Montana residence — 15% counts as rent-equivalent tax. Excludes mortgage payments, nursing home costs paid directly from Social Security, and rent paid by a rental assistance program

mtResided9Months.description: Schedule 2EC: the claimant resided in Montana at least nine months during the year

mtScheduleIvOtherTaxes.description: Form 2 line 19: contributions, penalties, interest and other taxes from Schedule IV line 8 — SUBTRACTED from total payments on line 21 rather than added to the tax

mtScheduleK1Withholding.description: Form 2 line 11d: total withholding from Montana Schedule(s) K-1, including mineral royalty withholding

mtSoleHouseholdClaimant.description: Schedule 2EC: you are the only member of your household claiming the elderly homeowner/renter credit — only one per household (unattested → not claimed)

mtSpouseAge65.description: Form 2 line 6: your spouse attained age 65 — a second $5,660 subtraction, on a JOINT return only (a qualifying surviving spouse has no spouse)

mtStateIncomeTaxAddback.description: Schedule I Part I line 4: state income tax included in federal ITEMIZED deductions, added back — computed on Worksheet B and capped so it never reduces the federal itemized total below the federal standard deduction (§ 15-30-2120(2)(j)). New placement for TY2025

mtTaxpayerAge65.description: Form 2 line 6: you attained age 65 — a $5,660 subtraction for 2025

mtTuitionSavingsContributions.description: Schedule I line 16: contributions to a Montana family education savings (§ 529) account — capped at $4,500, or $9,000 on a JOINT return, for 2025 (House Bill 845 raised it from $3,000)

ncBaileyRetirement.description: NC Schedule S line 20: Bailey settlement retirement benefits (NC/local government or US government incl. military retirees with 5+ years of creditable service as of Aug 12, 1989; state 401(k)/457 contributed before that date) — fully deducted; enclose the 1099-R

ncCharitable.description: NC Schedule A: IRC § 170 charitable contributions allowed for the year (no NC dollar cap)

ncClaimOfRightRepayment.description: NC Schedule A line 8: claim-of-right repayments over $3,000 (deducted in full)

ncMedicalExpenses.description: NC Schedule A line 7a: medical/dental expenses BEFORE the floor — the composer subtracts 7.5% of federal AGI

ncMilitaryRetirement.description: NC Schedule S line 21: military retirement pay / SBP payments for members with 20+ years of service OR Chapter 61 medical retirement — never severance, never double-claimed with Bailey

ncMortgageInterest.description: NC Schedule A: qualified mortgage interest — the composer applies the $20,000 combined cap with real estate taxes and takes itemized only when it beats the standard deduction

ncPartnershipPayments.description: D-400 line 21c: NC tax paid by a partnership on the filer's behalf

ncQualifyingChildren.description: D-400 line 10a: count of qualifying children for whom the federal § 24 child tax credit was ALLOWED (under 17; ODC-only dependents never count) — drives the AGI-tiered child deduction (us.nc.child_deduction)

ncRealEstateTaxes.description: NC Schedule A: real estate property taxes (NC allows NO income/sales tax deduction) — inside the $20,000 combined cap

ncScorpPayments.description: D-400 line 21d: NC tax paid by an S corporation on the filer's behalf

ncTaxCredits.description: D-400 line 16: D-400TC total (other-state credit worksheet, historic rehab) — hand-computed; the composer caps at the line 15 tax. NC has NO EITC and NO child/dependent care credit.

ncUnderpaymentInterest.description: D-400 line 26e: interest on the underpayment of estimated income tax (Form D-422)

ncUsObligationInterest.description: NC Schedule S line 18: interest from US obligations (Treasuries, savings bonds) included in FAGI — fully deducted

ncUseTaxEstimate.description: use the printed no-receipts consumer use tax table (keyed to line 14 taxable income, us.nc.use_tax) instead of the useTax input

ndAppliedToNextYear.description: Form ND-1 line 30: the amount of the line 29 overpayment to apply to 2026 estimated tax

ndCapitalGainAlreadyExcluded.description: Net long-term capital gain worksheet line 6: the portion of that gain already included on Form ND-1 line 7 or line 16, which is removed BEFORE the 40% is applied

ndCollegeSaveContributions.description: Form ND-1 line 12: contributions to a North Dakota College SAVE account (Bank of North Dakota) — capped at $5,000, or $10,000 on a JOINT return. Rollovers from another section 529 plan do NOT qualify

ndDoublyTaxedIncome.description: Schedule ND-1CR line 1c: the part of federal AGI sourced to the other state that was received or earned while a North Dakota resident

ndExemptTribalIncome.description: Form ND-1 line 7: exempt income of an enrolled member of a federally recognized tribe who lived on a North Dakota reservation all year (includes the North Dakota portions of Standing Rock and Lake Traverse that lie in South Dakota)

ndFederalTaxableIncome.description: REQUIRED for North Dakota. Form ND-1 line 1b: federal TAXABLE income from federal Form 1040 line 15 — North Dakota starts here, not from AGI. May be NEGATIVE: the booklet directs a filer whose federal taxable income calculates below zero to enter the negative number even though Form 1040 line 15 shows 0 — and gives Form ND-EZ line 1b the identical instruction

ndInterest.description: Form ND-1 line 34 box AL: interest

ndLowerQualifiedIncome.description: Marriage Penalty Credit Worksheet lines 3-4: the qualified income of the LOWER-earning spouse — wages and tips from federal line 1z, net self-employment income less the self-employment tax deduction, and the taxable IRA, pension, annuity and Social Security amounts, all reduced by the Form ND-1 line 8 and line 15 exclusions. Must exceed $47,550 for 2025

ndMilitaryPay.description: Form ND-1 line 11: military pay of a member of the armed forces on active or reserve duty or of the national guard, excluded IN FULL with no cap — including federal pay for training, education, mobilization and bonuses, and state pay on state active duty

ndMilitaryRetirement.description: Form ND-1 line 14: military retirement benefits, excluded IN FULL with no cap, for the retiree or a surviving spouse, and covering a dual-status military technician's federal civil-service retirement

ndNetLongTermCapitalGain.description: Net long-term capital gain worksheet line 3: the SMALLER of federal Schedule D lines 15 and 16 — or the capital gain distributions from Form 1040 line 7 when no Schedule D was required. North Dakota excludes 40%. The worksheet stops if either Schedule D figure is zero or less, so a net loss gives no exclusion

ndOtherStateIncomeBase.description: Schedule ND-1CR line 2: the ratio denominator. Defaults to federal AGI less the line 5 United States obligation interest, which is the printed full-year-resident rule; a part-year resident uses Schedule ND-1NR line 18 instead

ndOtherStateTaxPaid.description: Schedule ND-1CR line 6: the NET income tax on the other state's return — after that state's credits but before its withholding and estimated payments — plus local jurisdiction tax in that same state. A separate Schedule ND-1CR is required per state. Montana and Minnesota WAGES are excluded by reciprocity; foreign country tax never qualifies

ndPeaceOfficerRetirement.description: Form ND-1 line 9: the licensed peace officer retirement benefit exclusion — 20 years of licensed service or medical retirement for disability, employer plan benefits only

ndPenalty.description: Form ND-1 line 34 box AK: penalty

ndPlannedGiftAdjustment.description: Form ND-1 line 2: the planned gift or endowment tax credit adjustment to income, from Schedule ND-1PG line 15 or Schedule ND-1QEC line 16 — an ADDITION, because the contribution that earned the credit also reduced federal taxable income

ndQualifiedDividends.description: Form ND-1 line 13: qualified dividends from federal Form 1040 line 3a — North Dakota excludes 40%

ndRailroadRetirementBenefits.description: Form ND-1 line 8: Railroad Retirement Board benefits — unemployment, sick pay or retirement — to the extent federally taxable. Tier 1 Railroad Retirement belongs HERE, not on line 15

ndUnderpaymentInterest.description: Form ND-1 line 37: interest on underpaid estimated tax from Schedule ND-1UT — added into the line 36 balance due

ndUsObligationInterest.description: Form ND-1 line 5: interest from United States obligations. The booklet's enumerated list EXCLUDES Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, Ginnie Mae, federal tax refunds and repurchase agreements

ndUseRateSchedule.description: Form ND-1 line 20: apply the rate schedule at the exact taxable income instead of the printed Tax Table. Below $100,000 the table is MANDATORY by section 57-38-30.3(10); at $100,000 or more the schedule applies anyway

ndVoluntaryContributions.description: Form ND-1 line 31 (when overpaid) or line 35 (when tax is due): total voluntary contributions to the Veterans' Postwar Trust Fund, Watchable Wildlife Fund and Trees for ND Trust Fund

neAmendedOverpayment.description: NE line 54 (amended return only): overpayment allowed on the original return

neAmendedPaid.description: NE line 52 (amended return only): amount paid with the original return plus later payments

neChildCareExpenses.description: NE Form 2441N line 3 base (AGI $29,000 or less): qualified child/dependent care expenses paid, capped at $3,000 / $6,000 by neChildCareQualifyingPersons

neChildCareQualifyingPersons.description: NE Form 2441N qualifying persons (1 → $3,000 cap; 2 or more → $6,000); defaults to 1

neCommunityCollegeTaxes.description: NE line 45 (Form PTC line 2a → line 1): community college property taxes paid in 2025 on parcels you own — 100% refundable credit (the school district credit ended with LB 34; use the DOR Look-up Tool)

neCreditForward.description: NE line 61: overpayment applied to 2026 estimated tax

neEarnedIncome.description: NE Form 2441N line 4: the taxpayer's earned income

neFederalChildCareCredit.description: NE line 23: the federal child and dependent care credit (Schedule 3 line 2) — 25% nonrefundable when AGI is over $29,000

neFederalElderlyCredit.description: NE line 20: the federal credit for the elderly or the disabled (Schedule R, Schedule 3 line 6d) — Nebraska allows the same amount, nonrefundable

neFederalItemized.description: NE lines 7-10: the filer itemized on the federal return — Nebraska then allows the LARGER of its standard deduction and federal itemized deductions minus state and local income taxes (pass neFederalItemizedDeductions and neSaltIncomeTaxes). A federal standard-deduction filer must use the Nebraska standard deduction

neFederalItemizedDeductions.description: NE line 7: federal Schedule A line 17 total itemized deductions

neFederalOtherTax.description: NE line 16c: federal Form 4972 lump-sum tax plus federal Form 5329 early-distribution tax (the lesser of Form 5329 or Schedule 2 line 8) — Nebraska adds 29.6%

neFederalStandardDeduction.description: NE line 6, REQUIRED when claimedAsDependent or neSpouseClaimedAsDependent (line 2b): the federal standard deduction actually allowed (Form 1040 line 12e) — the Nebraska deduction is the smaller of it and the chart amount

neFederalTaxBeforeCredits.description: NE line 35 Federal Tax Liability Worksheet line 3: Form 1040 line 16 + Schedule 2 line 2 + Schedule 2 line 8 — when net Schedule I adjustments (line 12 − 13) are under $5,000, Nebraska tax after nonrefundable credits cannot exceed this (§ 77-2715(1)). Omitted, the cap is skipped with a note

neK1nWithholding.description: NE line 38: Nebraska income tax withheld reported on Schedules K-1N

neLocalUseTaxRate.description: NE line 58: your local sales and use tax rate in percent from the codes schedule (0.5, 1, 1.5, 1.75, or 2); omit for none

neMilitaryRetirement.description: NE Schedule I line 32: military retirement benefits in federal AGI (Form 1040 line 5b, DoD or OPM 1099-R) — 100% excluded

neNestContributions.description: NE Schedule I line 20: contributions by the account owner to Nebraska Educational Savings Plan Trust (NEST / Bloomwell / State Farm 529) accounts — the composer caps at $10,000 ($5,000 MFS)

neOtherStateAgi.description: NE Schedule II line 2: adjusted gross income derived from another state per the DOR Conversion Chart (not that state's taxable income)

neOtherStateTaxPaid.description: NE Schedule II line 5: income tax due and paid to the other state (or its political subdivision) — not withholding; no foreign taxes; attach the other state's complete return

nePtetCredit.description: NE line 39: pass-through entity tax (PTET) credit from Schedules K-1N

neSaltIncomeTaxes.description: NE line 8: state and local INCOME taxes on federal Schedule A line 5a (before the federal cap); $0 if line 5a is general sales taxes

neSpouseClaimedAsDependent.description: NE line 4b: the spouse can be claimed as another taxpayer's dependent — no exemption for the spouse

neSpouseEarnedIncome.description: NE Form 2441N line 5: the spouse's earned income (MFJ)

neStateRefund.description: NE Schedule I line 14: state income tax refund included in federal AGI (Schedule 1 line 1)

neStillbornChildren.description: NE line 47: stillborn children (20+ weeks, Nebraska certificate attached) — $2,000 each, refundable

neUnderpaymentPenalty.description: NE line 56: Form 2210N penalty for underpayment of estimated tax

neUsInterest.description: NE Schedule I lines 15-17: interest and RIC dividends from U.S. government obligations exempt from state tax

neUseTaxPurchases.description: NE line 58: 2025 taxable purchases on which no Nebraska sales tax was collected (Internet / out-of-state) — 5.5% state plus the local rate

neUseTaxTable.description: NE line 15: compute from the paper Nebraska Tax Table (row midpoints, endpoint worksheet over $77,760) instead of the Tax Calculation Schedule e-filers must use — they differ by up to $3 (the table prices each $100 row at its midpoint)

neVolunteerResponders.description: NE line 46: qualified volunteer emergency responders on the return certified to DOR for at least two years (0-2) — $250 each, refundable

neWildlifeDonation.description: NE line 62: Wildlife Conservation Fund donation from the overpayment ($1 or more)

neWithholding1099.description: NE line 37: Nebraska income tax withheld on W-2G, 1099-R, 1099-MISC, 1099-NEC (W-2 withholding goes in stateWithholding → line 36)

njAbcaAdjustment.description: NJ-1040 line 35 Alternative Business Calculation Adjustment (Schedule NJ-BUS-2 line 11 — the only cross-category loss softener, 20-year carryforward)

njAlimonyPaid.description: NJ-1040 line 32 court-ordered alimony PAID (still deductible for NJ; never child support)

njAlimonyReceived.description: NJ-1040 line 25 alimony received (NJ did not adopt the TCJA repeal — still NJ income)

njArcherMsa.description: Archer MSA contributions (federal Form 8853; NJ has NO HSA deduction — never enter HSA amounts)

njBaitCredit.description: NJ-1040 line 63 pass-through Business Alternative Income Tax credit (PTE-K-1)

njConservationContribution.description: NJ-1040 line 33 qualified conservation contribution (NJ land, federal amount)

njDispositionNet.description: NJ-1040 line 19 net gains from disposition of property (Schedule NJ-DOP; NO capital-gain preference, NO loss carryover; negative allowed — suppressed)

njEitcAgeDecoupled.description: flat-$260 NJEITC attested: 18+, no qualifying child, met all federal EIC requirements except age, not claimed as a dependent (NJ eliminated both federal age limits)

njExcessDi.description: NJ-1040 line 60 excess disability insurance withheld (over $380.42; NJ-2450)

njExcessFli.description: NJ-1040 line 61 excess family leave insurance withheld (over $545.82; NJ-2450)

njExcessUiWfSwf.description: NJ-1040 line 59 excess UI/WF/SWF withheld (two+ employers over $184.02; Form NJ-2450)

njFederalCdcc.description: the federal Form 2441 child and dependent care credit — enables the line 64 NJ CDCC (us.nj.cdcc: 50%→10% of it by NJ taxable income, $150,000 cap)

njGamblingNet.description: NJ-1040 line 24 net gambling winnings (losses net WITHIN the category; NJ Lottery prizes of $10,000 or less are exempt)

njGoldStarCredit.description: NJ-1040 line 47 Gold Star Family Counseling Credit (hours × TRICARE rate)

njHezDeduction.description: NJ-1040 line 34 Health Enterprise Zone deduction (TB-56)

njMedicalExpenses.description: unreimbursed medical expenses (Worksheet F line 1) — the composer applies the 2%-of-line-29 floor

njMfsSameHome.description: MFS and both spouses maintained the SAME main home — halves the property-tax deduction cap ($7,500) and credit ($25)

njNjbestContributions.description: NJ-1040 line 37a NJBEST 529 contributions (composer caps at $10,000; all three 37a-c require gross income ≤ $200,000)

njNjclassPaid.description: NJ-1040 line 37b NJCLASS loan principal+interest paid (composer caps at $2,500)

njOrganDonationExpenses.description: NJ-1040 line 36 organ/bone-marrow donation expenses (composer caps at $10,000)

njOrganDonorEmployerCredit.description: NJ-1040 line 48 employer of organ/bone-marrow donor credit (25% of salary, up to 30 days)

njOtherRetirementEligible.description: line 28b Worksheet D gate: filer is 62 or older (the composer auto-computes the unclaimed exclusion when earned income ≤ $3,000 and line 27 ≤ $100,000)

njOtherRetirementExclusion.description: OVERRIDE: hand-computed Worksheet D line 9 unclaimed exclusion (required for the $100,001-$150,000 percentage tiers)

njPartnershipNet.description: NJ-1040 line 21 distributive share of partnership income (NJK-1; negative suppressed)

njPension.description: NJ-1040 line 20a TAXABLE pension/annuity/IRA distributions (NJ three-year rule / general rule basis recovery already applied; Social Security and Railroad Retirement are exempt and never entered)

njPensionEligible.description: line 28a gate: filer (or spouse if joint) was 62+ OR blind/disabled per Social Security guidelines on the last day of the year — enables the pension exclusion (us.nj.pension_exclusion)

njPensionExcludable.description: NJ-1040 line 20b excludable (previously-taxed) pension/annuity/IRA amounts — display only
